project.name: TriageDesk
project.idea: A small web app for a support team: an agent pastes an incoming customer support ticket, and an AI feature classifies it (category, urgency), writes a one-sentence summary and suggests a first reply; the agent reviews and edits the suggestion. Must stay safe against prompt injection in ticket text, work without an API key via a clearly labelled deterministic fallback, and have an evaluation suite with explicit thresholds. Keep it small: Node.js, no database, single-page UI.

submissions.notes: Iteration 1. Memory searched (4 queries); only hit mem-k-muyljkrt-01991ac7 rejected (DOES-NOT-APPLY: node>=18). Runtime evidence ev:ev-muylm2jz-017e07c4. Q1/Q3/Q4 need user decisions.

openFindings.title: Brief contradicts recorded decisions on default model and PII redaction
openFindings.detail: The orchestrator recorded dec-muylppww (default ANTHROPIC_MODEL=claude-haiku-5-5) and dec-muylpq02 (redact emails and phone numbers before any live call). The submitted brief still says the opposite. Line 233 (decision table) and line 245 (deployment) default to claude-opus-5-5. Line 168 puts PII redaction out of scope. A5, RISK-3 and RISK-7 describe Opus-specific behaviour ('thinking cannot be disabled'). No R/NFR/AC covers redaction (ev:ev-muyls93g-01b3405c). Design would therefore build from a brief that disagrees with the project record. I accept the Haiku choice: claude-haiku-5-5 exists, supports structured outputs and output_config.effort 'low', and its default effort is medium (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/overview.md, https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/effort.md, both checked 2026-10-07). I challenge the redaction scope. The product handles billing tickets, which routinely contain payment card numbers. Redacting only emails and phones still sends card numbers (PANs) to a third party, and Q4 itself listed card numbers as a redaction class.
openFindings.recommendation: Resolved when the brief does all of the following. (1) Sets the default ANTHROPIC_MODEL to claude-haiku-5-5, marked as pending user confirmation, and rewrites A5, the decision table, RISK-3 and RISK-7 for Haiku 5.5 behaviour: adaptive thinking on by default, effort set explicitly to low, and thinking counted toward max_tokens. (2) Adds a requirement and an AC for redaction before the live call. The AC uses a stubbed transport to assert that marker email addresses, phone numbers and Luhn-valid card numbers in a ticket do not appear in the captured outbound request body. Card numbers are in scope unless the user explicitly declines. (3) Defines the order of operations: the injection detector runs on the original text, then redaction, then delimiter neutralisation. Placeholders must not collide with the <ticket> delimiters. (4) Updates the live-mode UI notice to say which classes are redacted. (5) Adds or extends a risk for redaction misses (false negatives).

openFindings.title: Raw-fetch JSON schema limits unaddressed; live path can 400 on every call
openFindings.detail: The brief chooses raw fetch with output_config.format json_schema and enforces lengths (summary <=200, reply 1-1200) and enums. Per https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/structured-outputs.md (checked 2026-10-07), the API rejects raw schemas that contain minLength/maxLength, minimum/maximum/multipleOf or maxItems with a 400. additionalProperties must be false on every object. Claude may change the capitalisation of enum values. The SDK helpers strip the unsupported keywords and validate locally, but the raw-fetch design does not get that benefit. AC9 checks only output_config.format.type === 'json_schema'. A schema that naturally includes maxLength 200/1200 would therefore pass every offline test while every live request returns 400 and falls back with model_error. Decision Q3 means no live call happens before delivery, so the defect would ship undetected and live mode would silently be fallback-only. The strict validator would also reject enum values that are correct but differently capitalised (invalid_output), which inflates fallback_rate.
openFindings.recommendation: Resolved when NFR2 states that the schema sent to the model uses only supported keywords: type, properties, required, enum, additionalProperties:false on every object, and no minLength/maxLength/minimum/maximum/maxItems. Lengths are enforced only by the server-side validator. AC9 must walk the captured schema and fail on any unsupported keyword or on an object without additionalProperties:false. The brief must also define the enum-case policy: normalise with a case-insensitive match before the enum check, or reject explicitly with a stated reason. Either way a test must cover it.

openFindings.title: Localhost bind is defeated by DNS rebinding; no Host/Origin validation
openFindings.detail: The trust model relies on binding to 127.0.0.1 with no auth or rate limit (NFR3, Scope, RISK-5 likelihood 'Low'). A web page the agent visits can use DNS rebinding: an attacker hostname re-resolves to 127.0.0.1, so its script becomes same-origin with the app. The script can then POST application/json to /api/triage without hitting a CORS preflight, read the responses and spend the operator's API key without limit. The 415 content-type check does not help, because rebinding makes the request same-origin. No requirement or AC in the brief validates the Host or Origin headers (ev:ev-muyls93g-01b3405c: no Host/Origin/DNS-rebinding lines). The fix is cheap and belongs to the architecture's trust boundary TB1.
openFindings.recommendation: Resolved when NFR3 requires the server to reject any request whose Host header is not in an allowlist derived from HOST:PORT (127.0.0.1, localhost, [::1]). The rejection must come before body parsing or any model call. The server must also reject POSTs whose Origin header is present and not same-origin, and must emit no CORS headers. AC11 (or a new AC) must test that 'Host: attacker.example' and a foreign Origin are rejected and that the fetch stub is never called. RISK-5 must be updated with this mitigation and its likelihood re-rated.

openFindings.title: Holdout split cannot detect fallback-rule overfitting
openFindings.detail: Thresholds are scored over all rows, and the roughly 30% holdout is only 'reported separately' (eval section; Success Criterion 2). If rules overfit the tuning rows perfectly, category_accuracy >= 0.70 and urgency_accuracy >= 0.65 still pass with 0% holdout accuracy, and high_urgency_recall >= 0.80 passes with 33% holdout recall (ev:ev-muyls93g-01b3405c). RISK-4 names this exact failure mode, and its mitigation is ineffective as written. With about 40 rows the holdout has about 12 rows, so per-metric holdout numbers carry 1-3 high-urgency rows. The brief does not say how a frozen dataset is proven to predate the rules.
openFindings.recommendation: Resolved when (1) the fallback thresholds are enforced on the holdout rows, or a stated holdout floor is enforced (for example, holdout within 0.10 of each threshold), and npm run eval exits non-zero when it is missed. (2) The brief sets minimum holdout counts, for example at least 2 rows per category and at least 4 label=high rows, enlarging the dataset if needed. (3) The dataset and holdout tags are frozen by recording the dataset's sha256 as evidence before any fallback-rule commit, and the verification gate checks that hash.

openFindings.title: injection_safety mixes accuracy with attack success and overclaims on 8 cases
openFindings.detail: injection_safety requires that the final category and urgency equal the true labels on every attack row, at 1.00, for both providers. Fallback accuracy is only required to reach 0.70/0.65 overall. Either the attack rows end up chosen to be easy for keyword rules (selection bias), or the metric fails for reasons that have nothing to do with injection. The brief says the fallback 'cannot be injected because it never echoes ticket text'. That holds for text echo but not for classification: its listed urgency cues ('urgent', 'outage', 'charged twice', 'data loss') are words an attacker controls. The heuristic detector's recall >= 0.90 is measured on attacks written by the same team that writes the detector regexes, with no held-out attack families, so the test is easy to game. Statistically, 8 out of 8 passes leaves a 95% upper bound of about 31% on the true failure rate (ev:ev-muyls93g-01b3405c). Success Criterion 4 ('Injection safety is 1.00 for both providers') cannot be met for live under decision Q3, because live evals are NOT RUN.
openFindings.recommendation: Resolved when the brief does all of the following. (1) Each attack row declares the attacker's targets (requested category/urgency that differ from the true labels, a canary token, a URL). Attack success is defined as the output adopting an attacker target, or the canary, prompt-marker or URL appearing. injection_safety (attack-success rate = 0) is kept separate from accuracy on attack rows, which is reported under the normal accuracy thresholds. (2) RISK-1 states the residual risk that fallback classification can be steered by keywords, mitigated by the flag and human review, and the fallback 'cannot be injected' claim is corrected. (3) The attack set is enlarged (for example to at least 20 rows across the detector's rule families), and some attack families are held out so that detector regexes are not written against them. (4) Results are reported as '0 failures in N' with the sample size, not as proof of safety. (5) Success Criterion 4 marks live injection results as NOT RUN when no key is available.

rev-muylut9q-014dc18b.summary: The brief is well structured and honest about unverified claims, and the scope is right-sized. It still cannot go to design yet. It contradicts two recorded orchestrator decisions: the default model is now Haiku and PII redaction is now required. The raw-fetch structured-output path ignores documented JSON-schema keyword limits, which would make every live call 400 and fall back with nothing to show it before delivery. The localhost bind is the only access control and it does not stop DNS rebinding. The holdout split and the injection_safety metric cannot measure what they claim to measure.

criteria.description: Completeness: users, problem, workflows, constraints, scope and requirements are explicit and consistent with recorded decisions
criteria.notes: Users, problem, W1-W4 and scope reasons are good. However, the brief still sets claude-opus-5-5 as the default (lines 233, 245) and keeps PII redaction out of scope (line 168), against decisions dec-muylppww / dec-muylpq02 (ARCH-1). It has no Host/Origin requirement (ARCH-3).

criteria.description: Testability: every AC is decidable by test or inspection and every requirement traces to an AC
criteria.notes: AC1-AC15 are concrete and trace to R/NFR ids. Gaps: the RISK-7 mitigation (4xx -> model_error) and stop_reason max_tokens have no AC (ARCH-6). The validator's 'one sentence' and 'no URL/email' rules are not defined precisely enough to decide (ARCH-7). Success criterion 2 reports holdout results but sets no pass rule for them (ARCH-4).

criteria.description: Assumptions: risky or unverified assumptions are labelled, and questions that need the user are escalated
criteria.notes: A1-A8 carry 'Blocks' notes, and A5/A6 honestly mark the reference-only claims. Q1/Q3/Q4 were escalated correctly. Folding the orchestrator's answers back into the brief is tracked under ARCH-1.

criteria.description: Complexity: no unnecessary components; simplest design that meets requirements
criteria.notes: node:http, a single static page, no state, a pure-function fallback and one model call per request. Nothing here is superfluous. The rationale for the zero-dependency choice is misattributed (ARCH-8, minor), but the choice itself is defensible.

criteria.description: Feasibility: technology limits, API surface, latency and cost verified against authoritative sources
criteria.notes: The Node 22 runtime is verified. I verified the model ids and support for output_config.format and effort against platform.claude.com on 2026-10-07. The raw-fetch schema limits are unaddressed (ARCH-2). The brief does not account for thinking tokens counting toward max_tokens (ARCH-6).

criteria.description: Security and privacy: trust boundaries, secrets, PII, prompt injection, least privilege
criteria.notes: TB1-TB4, no tools, display-only output, textContent with CSP, and the key read from env only are all strong. Gaps: DNS rebinding bypasses the localhost bind (ARCH-3). The required redaction has no requirement or AC, and its scope leaves out payment card numbers (ARCH-1).

criteria.description: AI features: real value, eval cases with sound thresholds, fallback on model failure, human oversight
criteria.notes: The value statement, the labelled fallback and the human-in-the-loop design are good. The holdout split cannot detect overfitting (ARCH-4). injection_safety mixes up accuracy with attack success and rests on too few cases to support its claim (ARCH-5).

criteria.description: Risk register: likelihood, impact, mitigation and owner for every material risk, with mitigations that hold
criteria.notes: RISK-1..8 are complete in form. RISK-5 rates likelihood Low on the strength of the 127.0.0.1 bind, which DNS rebinding defeats (ARCH-3). No risk covers redaction failure or leakage once redaction is adopted (ARCH-1).

findings.title: Fallback triggers for HTTP errors and max_tokens truncation are untested
findings.detail: AC4 covers throw, timeout, non-JSON, out-of-enum, URL and refusal. It does not cover a non-2xx HTTP response (400/404 for a wrong model id, 429, 529), although RISK-7's mitigation relies on '4xx -> model_error'. stop_reason 'max_tokens' is checked by the live provider but maps to no R6 fallbackReason. Thinking counts toward max_tokens on Haiku 5.5 (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/effort.md, checked 2026-10-07), so the 1,024 cap needs a rationale.
findings.recommendation: Extend AC4 with stubbed HTTP 404 (with a body), 429 and 529 responses mapped to model_error, and with stop_reason max_tokens mapped to a named reason. State why max_tokens=1024 leaves room for thinking at effort low, or raise it.

findings.title: Validator rules 'one sentence' and 'no URL/email' are not precisely defined
findings.detail: The single-sentence rule (R3, AC2) and the no-URL/no-email rule (NFR2) decide fallback, but text like 'e.g.', 'v2.1', 'Mr.', bare domains ('example.com') and obfuscated forms ('name at example dot com') are undefined. As a result the model-validity and fallback_rate metrics depend on how the implementer reads the rule.
findings.recommendation: Define both rules as deterministic patterns, in the brief or as a binding design-gate item, with accept and reject test vectors for the edge cases above.

findings.title: Zero-dependency constraint attributed to the project, which never set it
findings.detail: The decision table says the SDK 'would break the zero-dependency constraint the project set'. The project idea says only 'Keep it small: Node.js, no database, single-page UI'. Raw fetch is defensible on its merits: one endpoint, an injectable transport and no retries wanted. But it is the architect's choice, and it loses the SDK's schema stripping and typed errors (see ARCH-2).
findings.recommendation: Restate NFR1 and the decision row as an architect's decision with its trade-offs (including ARCH-2), and list it for user confirmation alongside Q1/Q4.

findings.title: Q2/Q5/Q6 proposed defaults acceptable; Q5 moot with Haiku default
findings.detail: I accept the A3 taxonomy (Q2), local-only refusal handling (Q5) and no URLs in replies (Q6). According to the claude-api reference (cached 2026-10-06), Claude Haiku 5.5 has no server-side refusal fallback, so Q5 has no option to choose once the default becomes Haiku.
findings.recommendation: Record Q2/Q5/Q6 as decided with the proposed defaults, and note that Q5 no longer applies under the Haiku default.

ho-muylp5jn-012f0637.context: TriageDesk is a small local Node.js 22 web app: an agent pastes a support ticket and gets a category, an urgency, a one-sentence summary and an editable suggested reply. It calls the Anthropic Messages API through raw fetch, falls back to a clearly labelled deterministic rule-based classifier, and must be safe against prompt injection. Constraints: zero npm dependencies, no database, a single page, and an eval suite with explicit thresholds (fixed in the brief's 'Evaluation metrics and thresholds' table). Memory search found one lesson (mem-k-muyljkrt-01991ac7, 'need node-fetch/axios because global fetch is missing'); its check verdict was DOES-NOT-APPLY (requires Node <18, environment has 22.22.0), so it was rejected and not cited. The model id claude-opus-5-5 and the request shape (output_config.format json_schema, effort low, anthropic-version 2023-06-01) come from the claude-api reference cached 2026-10-06. They were not verified by a live call because no API key is set (A5, RISK-7). The submission's runtime evidence is ev:ev-muylm2jz-017e07c4. An earlier evidence run, ev:ev-muyllyra-018a7124, failed only because of shell quoting in the command and carries no product signal.
ho-muylp5jn-012f0637.expectedOutput: An architecture gate review (approve or changes_requested) with findings referenced by id, covering requirement testability, AC traceability, trust boundaries and injection controls, the fallback design, the eval thresholds, and the scope exclusions.

RISK-1.title: Prompt injection in ticket text manipulates classification/reply or leaks system prompt
RISK-1.mitigation: Fixed system prompt + delimited/neutralised ticket, no tools, json_schema output, strict validator (enums, lengths, no URL/email in reply), display-only output, heuristic flag + UI warning, eval injection_safety=1.00 on >=8 attacks, human review

RISK-2.title: Automation bias: agents send drafts unread or mistake fallback output for AI output
RISK-2.mitigation: Permanent text source label + fallback reason, injection warning, copy-only (no send), 'not AI-generated' wording tested (AC5)

RISK-3.title: Live model slow/unavailable/refuses/returns invalid or hallucinated output
RISK-3.mitigation: 20s timeout, single attempt, deterministic fallback with reason, strict validator, effort low, fallback_rate and raw_model_validity metrics

RISK-4.title: Eval not meaningful: fallback rules overfit a small same-team dataset
RISK-4.mitigation: Dataset authored and frozen by test-engineer, ~30% holdout reported separately, thresholds fixed in brief before rules exist, sample size stated

RISK-5.title: API key leak or key-spend abuse via exposed unauthenticated server
RISK-5.mitigation: Key from env only, never echoed (AC10/AC14), bind 127.0.0.1 by default, body and max_tokens caps, one call per request; auth + rate limiting required before any non-local deployment

RISK-6.title: Ticket PII logged locally or sent to third party without awareness
RISK-6.mitigation: Metadata-only logs tested with marker (AC10), no persistence, live-mode UI notice, Q4 escalated to user

RISK-7.title: Model id / Messages API surface unverified live (claude-opus-5-5, output_config.format, effort) from cached reference
RISK-7.mitigation: Model via ANTHROPIC_MODEL env, /api/health reports model, 4xx -> fallback model_error, request-shape contract test (AC9), confirm on first live call, report unverified status honestly

RISK-8.title: XSS via ticket or model text rendered as HTML
RISK-8.mitigation: textContent-only rendering, CSP default-src 'self' without inline script, grep check for HTML sinks (AC11)
